texts.preamble: M/S Sky Line vs The State Of Telangana on 4 September, 2025
texts.facts: This writ petition is filed seeking following prayer:- "to declare the action of the 5th Respondent in not allowing the petitioner to serve flavored herbal hookah to the customers and also obstructing the business activities of the cafe and acting further in contravention of the principles of natural justice as illegal, arbitrary, and it is further prayed that this Honourable Court pending disposal of the writ petition may be pleased to direct the respondents not to obstruct the business activities of the petitioner and allow them to serve flavored herbal Hookah to the customers of his cafe." 2. Brief facts stated in this writ petition are that petitioner is a coffee shop running under the name and style of M/s.Sky Line, situated at Gundlapochampally, Kandlakoi Village, Medchal Malkajgiri District. It is stated that the petitioner, having acquired the statutory licenses from the competent authorities which includes registration of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, Municipal Trade License, Labour License, is running the said business. It is further stated that the said shop is also serving hooka to the customers. The case of the petitioner is that the respondent No.5 under Section 7(5) and 21(1) of COTPA Act 2003, registered FIR No.672 of 2025 dated 16.04.2025 against the petitioner and during the investigation visited the subject premises and seized the hookah pots. Thereafter, notice under Section 35(3)of BNSS was issued to the petitioner. It is further stated that petitioner has not violated any of the provisions of COTPA Act 2003. Further case of the petitioner is that the respondent authorities are entering the petitioner's subject premises and are threatening to seal the same. Aggrieved by the same, this writ petition is filed. The officers, who are competent alone can enter the premises.
texts.arguments: Though the Act does not contemplate any licence to be taken, in the larger interest of the youngsters, who are visiting the hookah centres, the restaurant owners shall have a definite place for hookah / smoking. The restaurant owners, who are having a separate place for smoking and for hookah consumption, shall inform the same to the Station House Officer, so that they can have surveillance on the activities that are taking place in the said place and whether the business is carried out as per the norms and the procedure laid down under the Act. Police under the guise of this, shall not harass the persons running these centers without following the procedure. Relying on the above, learned counsel for the petitioner pray this Court to grant liberty to petitioner to make representation before the respondent Police and seek permission to serve hookah at his cafe. The petitioner shall earmark exclusively a separate area with appropriate enclosure in the hotel premises and no other area or portion of the premises shall be used by the customers of the petitioner for smoking hookah." 8. It is also relevant to refer to the common order dated 15.11.2023 passed in W.P.Nos.8223 of 2013 and batch, relevant portion is extracted hereunder:- "ii) Since the Hyderabad City Police Act, 1348 Fasli confers power over the amusement Centres/restaurants which are defined as "public place" under the COTP Act and as per Rule 4 of the Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008 permission is required specifying smoking area.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Relying on the above, learned counsel for the petitioner pray this Court to grant liberty to petitioner to make representation before the respondent Police and seek permission to serve hookah at his cafe.
